THOUGHT: The patient is a severely immunosuppressed HIV-positive man (CD4 56/µL, high viral load) with a subacute (weeks–months) course of cognitive decline, behavioral change, somnolence, and new focal neurologic findings (right lower-extremity weakness, unsteady gait, falls). Brain MRI shows disseminated white-matter lesions that are nonenhancing and without mass effect. These findings strongly favor demyelinating infection from JC virus — progressive multifocal leukoencephalopathy (PML). Alternative diagnoses are less likely: cerebral toxoplasmosis typically causes multiple ring-enhancing lesions with mass effect (despite positive Toxo IgG, imaging is not consistent); primary CNS lymphoma usually gives enhancing, often periventricular mass lesions; cryptococcal disease would have other CSF/clinical features and cryptococcal antigen is negative; HIV-associated neurocognitive disorder can cause subcortical cognitive decline but usually lacks focal, asymmetric motor deficits and the characteristic nonenhancing multifocal white-matter lesions of PML. The combination of advanced immunosuppression, subacute focal deficits, progressive cognitive/behavioral changes, and MRI appearance makes PML the single most likely diagnosis. Confirmation would be by CSF JC virus PCR and neurology/infectious-disease evaluation.

DIAGNOSIS: Progressive multifocal leukoencephalopathy (JC virus reactivation)
